Trait subsets for the block estimator

Source: R/subsets.R
indri_subsets.Rd

Draws the trait subsets on which the small models are fitted. This is the set-cover construction used by LiMMBo from version 1.0 on: each subset is built from a window of trait pairs, and the number of subsets is chosen so that every pair is covered at least min_cooccurrence times.

Usage

indri_subsets(K, s, min_cooccurrence = 3L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

K

Number of traits.

s

Subset size parameter, at least 2. Controls how many trait pairs each subset covers.

min_cooccurrence

Minimum number of distinct subsets every trait pair must appear in.

seed

Optional seed for the subset construction. The caller's random state is left untouched.

Value

An integer matrix with one distinct subset per row, holding 1-based indices of the traits in that subset. Every pair is in at least min_cooccurrence distinct subsets, capped at the number of distinct subsets of this width that contain it (one, for two-trait subsets); the coverage reached is stored in the min_cooccurrence attribute and the pair counts in the coverage attribute.

Details

Three things differ from LiMMBo's implementation. The permutation that orders the pairs is seeded here, so the result is reproducible (LiMMBo draws it from the global numpy generator and is not), and the caller's random seed is restored afterwards. The coverage is guaranteed: LiMMBo's passes cover each pair only ceiling(min_cooccurrence / 2) times by construction and leave the rest to chance, which often falls short; indri adds greedily built subsets of the same width until every pair reaches min_cooccurrence. And coverage counts distinct subsets: a subset is never repeated, since a pair estimated twice in the same trait context adds nothing.

Note that the subset size is not exactly s. A subset covers s - 1 trait pairs, which is up to 2 * (s - 1) distinct traits; the subsets therefore come out larger than s, and the assembled blocks use ncol(subsets) rather than s.

Examples

subsets <- indri_subsets(K = 6, s = 3, min_cooccurrence = 3)
subsets
#>       [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#>  [1,]    1    3    4    5
#>  [2,]    1    2    4    6
#>  [3,]    2    3    4    5
#>  [4,]    2    3    4    6
#>  [5,]    1    3    5    6
#>  [6,]    1    2    4    5
#>  [7,]    3    4    5    6
#>  [8,]    1    2    3    6
#>  [9,]    1    2    3    5
#> [10,]    1    2    5    6
#> attr(,"coverage")
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#> [1,]    7    5    4    3    5    4
#> [2,]    5    7    4    4    4    4
#> [3,]    4    4    7    4    5    4
#> [4,]    3    4    4    6    4    3
#> [5,]    5    4    5    4    7    3
#> [6,]    4    4    4    3    3    6
#> attr(,"min_cooccurrence")
#> [1] 3
ncol(subsets)  # Actual block width; it can be larger than s.
#> [1] 4
coverage <- attr(subsets, "coverage")
coverage
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#> [1,]    7    5    4    3    5    4
#> [2,]    5    7    4    4    4    4
#> [3,]    4    4    7    4    5    4
#> [4,]    3    4    4    6    4    3
#> [5,]    5    4    5    4    7    3
#> [6,]    4    4    4    3    3    6
min(coverage[upper.tri(coverage)])
#> [1] 3
